concepts.name: Population versus sample
concepts.summary: Distinguish the whole group of interest from the subset actually measured, and recognise why we sample.

concepts.name: Types of variables
concepts.summary: Classify variables as categorical or numerical and explain which summaries suit each.

concepts.name: Mean, median and mode
concepts.summary: Compute and interpret the three measures of centre and say what each tells about a data set.

concepts.name: Range and spread
concepts.summary: Explain spread as how far values vary and compute the range as a simple measure of it.

concepts.name: Reading histograms
concepts.summary: Read a histogram to describe the shape, centre and spread of a numerical data set.

concepts.name: Five-number summary and boxplots
concepts.summary: Identify the minimum, quartiles, median and maximum and read them from a boxplot.

misconceptions.text: The mean is always the best description of the typical value.
A taller bar in a histogram means the value is larger rather than more frequent.
The median line in a boxplot sits at the centre of the box, and each quarter of the box holds the same number of values only by width.

concepts.name: Variance and standard deviation
concepts.summary: Calculate the standard deviation of a sample and interpret it as typical distance from the mean.

concepts.name: Skewness and outliers
concepts.summary: Identify skew and outliers in plots and predict their effect on the mean and median.

concepts.name: Interquartile range and outlier rule
concepts.summary: Compute the IQR and use the 1.5×IQR fences to flag outliers on a boxplot.

concepts.name: Random sampling methods
concepts.summary: Describe simple random, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling and when each is used.

concepts.name: Sampling bias
concepts.summary: Spot how a sampling procedure can systematically distort results, such as voluntary response or convenience samples.

concepts.name: Comparing distributions
concepts.summary: Compare two groups using centre, spread and shape from histograms or parallel boxplots.

misconceptions.text: A large sample automatically removes bias from a poorly designed sampling method.
Outliers should always be deleted from the data.
Standard deviation can be negative or measures the total distance of values from the mean.

concepts.name: Normal distribution and z-scores
concepts.summary: Use z-scores and the empirical rule to find proportions and percentiles under a normal model.

concepts.name: Sampling distribution of the mean
concepts.summary: Explain how sample means vary across repeated samples and how that distribution differs from the data distribution.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.summary: Analyse why sample means become approximately normal for large samples regardless of population shape.

concepts.name: Standard error
concepts.summary: Compute the standard error and show how it shrinks with sample size.

concepts.name: Confidence intervals for a mean
concepts.summary: Construct and interpret an interval estimate using the estimate, critical value and standard error.

concepts.name: Null and alternative hypotheses
concepts.summary: State null and alternative hypotheses, one- or two-sided, for a research question.

concepts.name: p-values and significance level
concepts.summary: Interpret a p-value as the probability of data this extreme under the null and compare it with alpha.

misconceptions.text: A 95% confidence interval contains 95% of the individual data values.
The p-value is the probability that the null hypothesis is true.
The central limit theorem says the data themselves become normal as the sample grows.

concepts.name: One-sample and two-sample t-tests
concepts.summary: Choose and carry out the right t-test for one mean or two independent means and interpret the t statistic.

concepts.name: Paired t-test
concepts.summary: Recognise paired designs and test the mean of the within-pair differences.

concepts.name: Chi-square test of independence
concepts.summary: Compute expected counts and the chi-square statistic to test association between two categorical variables.

concepts.name: Chi-square goodness of fit
concepts.summary: Test whether observed category counts match a hypothesised distribution.

concepts.name: Test assumptions and checks
concepts.summary: Evaluate independence, normality, equal variance and expected-count conditions and judge whether a test is valid.

concepts.name: Type I and Type II errors
concepts.summary: Distinguish the two error types and how significance level and sample size affect them.

concepts.name: Statistical power
concepts.summary: Judge how effect size, variability, alpha and sample size determine power and what that means for study design.

concepts.name: Statistical versus practical significance
concepts.summary: Evaluate whether a statistically significant result is large enough to matter, using effect sizes and intervals.

misconceptions.text: A non-significant result proves there is no effect.
A smaller p-value means a larger or more important effect.
A chi-square test shows that one variable causes the other.

concepts.name: Multiple comparisons problem
concepts.summary: Evaluate how running many tests inflates false positives and choose corrections such as Bonferroni or false discovery rate.

concepts.name: p-hacking and researcher degrees of freedom
concepts.summary: Critique analyses whose flexibility in choices invalidates reported p-values.

concepts.name: Bootstrap and permutation methods
concepts.summary: Design resampling procedures to estimate uncertainty or test hypotheses when parametric assumptions fail.

concepts.name: Interpretation of confidence intervals
concepts.summary: Evaluate the frequentist meaning of coverage and contrast it with Bayesian credible intervals.

concepts.name: Nonparametric alternatives
concepts.summary: Judge when rank-based tests are preferable to t-tests and what they actually test.

concepts.name: Study design and confounding
concepts.summary: Design studies with randomisation, control and blinding to support causal claims and handle confounders.

concepts.name: Replication and reporting
concepts.summary: Plan analyses and reports, including pre-registration, effect sizes and intervals, that hold up under replication.

misconceptions.text: If the test is run once on the final chosen analysis, earlier exploratory tests do not affect the p-value.
Bootstrapping can fix a biased or unrepresentative sample.
A particular computed 95% interval has a 95% probability of containing the true parameter.
